paragraphs.title: Jehoiakim's Rebellion and Pressure on Judah

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up in Jehoiakim's days.
easy.q: Who came up in the days of Jehoiakim?

easy.explanation: Jehoiakim became the servant of Babylon for three years, and then rebelled.
easy.q: How long was Jehoiakim the servant of the king of Babylon before he rebelled?

answers: The Chaldees, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites
easy.explanation: The passage names bands of the Chaldees, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites.
easy.q: What groups were sent against Judah?

answers: Jehoiakim's rebellion against the king of Babylon
medium.explanation: Jehoiakim rebelled against the king of Babylon, after which the bands were sent against Judah.
medium.q: What led to the sending of the bands against Judah?

medium.explanation: Bands were groups of armed men sent to act against Judah.
medium.q: In the phrase “bands of the Chaldees,” what does “bands” mean?

answers: The sins of Manasseh and the shedding of innocent blood
medium.explanation: The passage connects the judgment with Manasseh's sins and the innocent blood shed in Jerusalem.
medium.q: According to the passage, what was the deeper reason for the judgment upon Judah?

answers: It was understood as divine judgment, not merely a political war
challenge.explanation: The wording presents the events as the fulfillment of the LORD's word spoken through the prophets.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “according to the word of the LORD” suggest about the invasion?

answers: Egypt could no longer come out of its land to help
challenge.explanation: The king of Egypt came no more out of his land because Babylon had taken the territory as far as the Euphrates.
challenge.q: What does the passage reveal about Egypt at the end of this section?

answers: The events are presented as continuing judgment for Manasseh's sins and innocent bloodshed
The passage makes no connection between the past and the present
Past sins caused Judah to make a covenant with Egypt
challenge.explanation: The passage explains Judah's troubles partly as judgment for earlier sins and bloodshed.
challenge.q: How are past sins related to the events in Jehoiakim's reign?

paragraphs.title: Jehoiachin's Reign and the Siege of Jerusalem

easy.explanation: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign.
easy.q: How old was Jehoiachin when he began to reign?

easy.explanation: Jehoiachin reigned in Jerusalem for three months.
easy.q: How long did Jehoiachin reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar's servants came against Jerusalem, and Nebuchadnezzar himself came against the city.
easy.q: Who came against Jerusalem during Jehoiachin's reign?

answers: He went out to the king of Babylon
He rebelled against the princes of Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Jehoiachin went out to the king of Babylon with his household and officials.
medium.q: What did Jehoiachin do when Jerusalem was besieged?

answers: The king of Egypt and his army
His mother, servants, princes, and officers
medium.explanation: The verse lists his mother, servants, princes, and officers.
medium.q: Who went with Jehoiachin to the king of Babylon?

answers: The city surrendered immediately without opposition
The city was surrounded by enemy forces
medium.explanation: To besiege a city means to surround it with military forces.
medium.q: What does “the city was besieged” mean?

answers: Jerusalem enjoyed a long period of stability
The kingdom quickly came under Babylonian pressure and conquest
Jehoiachin established a broad and secure rule
challenge.explanation: He reigned only three months before Jerusalem was besieged and he was taken away.
challenge.q: What does Jehoiachin's brief reign suggest about Jerusalem's condition?

challenge.explanation: The passage says that the king of Babylon took Jehoiachin in the eighth year of his reign.
challenge.q: In what year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign was Jehoiachin taken?

answers: Submission by the king and those with him
challenge.explanation: Jehoiachin went out to Babylon's king and was then taken captive with those who accompanied him.
challenge.q: What did Jehoiachin's going out to the king of Babylon signify in the context of the siege?

paragraphs.title: The Plundering of the Treasures and Deportation of the Elites

answers: Only the treasures of private citizens
The treasures of the house of the LORD and the king's house
easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar took the treasures of the LORD's house and the king's house.
easy.q: Which treasures did the king of Babylon take from Jerusalem?

answers: The princes, mighty men, craftsmen, and smiths
easy.explanation: The passage lists the princes, mighty men, craftsmen, and smiths among those taken.
easy.q: Who was carried away from Jerusalem?

answers: The poorest sort of the people of the land
easy.explanation: None remained except the poorest sort of the people of the land.
easy.q: Who remained in the land after the deportation?

answers: He cut them in pieces and took them away
He gave them to the princes of Judah
medium.explanation: He cut in pieces the golden vessels Solomon had made and removed them from the temple.
medium.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar do to the vessels of gold made by Solomon?

answers: To weaken the strength and abilities of the people left behind
medium.explanation: Removing skilled workers and soldiers weakened the remaining population.
medium.q: Why would the craftsmen and smiths have been deported, according to the passage's meaning?

medium.explanation: A craftsman is a person skilled in making or repairing things.
medium.q: In this context, what is a “craftsman”?

answers: He sought to weaken Judah's resources, military power, and skilled workforce
He sought to strengthen Jerusalem's independence
He gave up control of Judah
challenge.explanation: Taking the treasures and capable people weakened Judah materially and practically.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Nebuchadnezzar taking both the treasures and the soldiers and craftsmen?

answers: The passage mentions seven thousand men of might and those apt for war
The passage mentions only women and children
challenge.explanation: Seven thousand men of might and those strong and apt for war were taken captive.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the deportation included people with military ability?

challenge.explanation: The king of Babylon carried them into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
challenge.q: Where were most of the people described in this section taken?

paragraphs.title: Zedekiah and Judah's Rebellion against Babylon

easy.explanation: The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's father's brother, king in his stead.
easy.q: Whom did the king of Babylon make king instead of Jehoiachin?

easy.explanation: The king of Babylon changed Mattaniah's name to Zedekiah.
easy.q: What new name did the king of Babylon give Mattaniah?

easy.explanation: Zedekiah reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years.
easy.q: How long did Zedekiah reign in Jerusalem?

answers: He did that which was right in the sight of the LORD
He did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD
It says nothing about his conduct
medium.explanation: The passage says that Zedekiah did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD.
medium.q: What does the passage say about Zedekiah's conduct?

medium.explanation: Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

answers: He gave Mattaniah a different name
He sent Mattaniah back to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The king of Babylon changed Mattaniah's name to Zedekiah.
medium.q: In context, what does “changed his name” mean?

answers: Babylon exercised direct authority over Judah's leadership
Mattaniah was chosen by all the people without outside involvement
challenge.explanation: The appointment and name change were performed by the Babylonian king, showing his control.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the king of Babylon appointing Mattaniah and changing his name?

answers: Both are presented as part of Judah's continued disobedience
The rebellion is presented as a change for the better
challenge.explanation: Zedekiah is described as doing evil, and he eventually rebelled against Babylon as well.
challenge.q: How are Zedekiah's evil conduct and his rebellion related in the passage?

answers: Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah
challenge.explanation: Zedekiah's mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
